summary: Nudge a seat that sits idle holding claimed work with nothing set to wake it, once, naming the step and its waits, and record the nudge on the step

replay.detail: No shared projection replay is needed. A new disposable local message index is populated during first startup and maintained on claim writes; reads never populate or rebuild it.

schema.detail: Two additive lookup indexes select watches by recipient and report-to runs by reporter. local_idle_messages is a disposable local table with two indexes and four versioned triggers on shared claims: local_idle_messages_sent_v1, local_idle_messages_receipt_v1, local_idle_messages_delete_v1 and local_idle_messages_update_v1. Sent/delete/update fold the message; inserted receipts only update pending/delivered flags by primary key, avoiding sent-body reads. The wake index covers only delivered messages carrying a source prefix. The trigger bodies have no INDEXED BY dependency; the existing claims_subject_kind_index and claims_subject_kind_accepted_index are ordinary planner choices, so removing or renaming one does not invalidate claim writes. Schema setup removes the earlier unversioned trigger names. Startup backfill commits at most 64 message subjects per transaction and resumes after interruption; cursor removal and the idempotent completion marker share one transaction. No shared tables or columns change. The claim vocabulary gains work.nudged (system-only, append, on step-run) with optional attempt, agent, message, idle_since_unix_ms, reason and waits fields. The client contract adds optional nudged_at_unix_ms to work and nudged_at to mission steps.

rules.detail: Checkpoint rules and their digests are unchanged. The claim registry digest changes with the new kind, as with any vocabulary addition: members on different builds keep replicating claims and skip comparing projection maps until all are upgraded.

compatibility.detail: A member on an older build does not know work.nudged, so it holds a replicated nudge as unknown and admits it after it upgrades. A seat on an older host is never nudged, because only the host that runs a seat evaluates it. [reconcile] gains idle_nudge_after (default 30m, or off) and idle_nudge_quiet_watch (default 2h). A config that sets either one fails to load on an older build, because [reconcile] denies unknown fields. Not tested against an older build.

downtime.detail: First startup creates the additive lookup indexes before requests are admitted. CREATE INDEX holds the SQLite writer during creation. On a copy of the 200,790-claim benchmark store with 700 declarations, five report-index creations including commit had a 69.4 ms median and 1,980.7 ms maximum; watch-index creation had a 19.6 ms median and 19.8 ms maximum. The initial report-index execution alone took 92.8 ms, and a concurrent writer was refused during it. These are measured startup costs, not bounds for larger stores. Three budgeted local message-index backfills of 5,125 messages measured 1,454.3 ms median / 1,460.3 ms maximum, with a 36.4 ms maximum writer batch and 35.1 ms maximum commit. Batches stop after 64 subjects or 20 ms of processing. An earlier three-run control without the elapsed processing budget had a 250.5 ms writer-transaction outlier under host load; storage and scheduling can exceed the processing budget, so it is not a hard wall-time bound. Restart after successful backfill only checks its marker. Idle checks run in the existing incremental seat wake evaluation and register their next deadlines; they add no sampler or polling thread. Pending mailbox and child-seat reads happen only when a nudge can be sent. Linear extrapolation of the measured warm message backfill gives about 4.5 seconds for 16,000 subjects and 7.9 seconds for 28,000 subjects (the earlier 1.15-second backfill implied 3.6-6.3 seconds); production density and cold-cache startup are unmeasured. A backfill failure still aborts startup rather than admitting idle checks against incomplete pending-mail state; the committed cursor supports retry.

manual.detail: On by default. Turn it off with idle_nudge_after = "off" under [reconcile]; the daemon reads it again within two minutes. The guide is in docs/st3/mission-graph-runtime.md under Idle holders.

recovery.detail: Swap back to the previous binary after removing any newly configured reconcile fields. Nudges stop, and work.nudged claims stay in the graph unread. SQLite triggers persist in the database file: older binaries continue executing the four local_idle_messages_*_v1 triggers on message claim writes and maintaining the local table. Keep the table while those triggers exist; dropping the table makes claims writes fail when their statements are prepared. The trigger bodies no longer require either named claims index to exist. To rebuild the disposable cache, stop the daemon, delete local_idle_messages rows and the meta keys local_idle_messages_v1 and local_idle_messages_backfill_after in one transaction, then restart the newer binary. Never drop the table while its triggers exist. An interrupted backfill resumes from its committed cursor.
